correctness.rationale: Normalize by z=au+ibv on the unit disk. The squared disk radius has the Beta(1,α+1) law; angular averaging gives second moments 1/(2s), single-coordinate fourth moments 3/[4s(s+1)] and the mixed fourth moment 1/[4s(s+1)]. Central symmetry and subtraction of c²/(2s) in degree two give the orthogonal basis and squared norms c²R/(2s) and c⁴D/[4s²(s+1)]. In the resulting quartic diagonal, the angular penalty B−A is positive and the coefficient A of x² has the sign of P. If P≥0 only the origin achieves the lower bound, and when P=0 the real-axis expansion starts with a positive quartic. If P<0, completing the square gives C(x²+y²−x_*²)²+(B−A)y² above the minimum, with x_*²=−A/(2C). This vanishes only at the two real sites; −P<2(s+1)R puts both strictly inside the ellipse. Subtracting A²/(4C) gives the stated minimum. P(1)=−3, P has exactly one positive root, and R increases with b/a; the stated critical examples follow by substitution. The reciprocal has the same maximizing sites. This proof applies to the complex analytic space through degree two, not the real bivariate or infinite Bergman kernel.
